labelOrigin: Agent-drafted from reading the code at the pinned commit (CLA-289); pending Brenton's spot-check before counting as ground truth.

questions.question: What happens on the server when someone publishes a new gem release from the command line?
questions.answerNote: Api::V1::RubygemsController#create checks the API key can push, then Pusher#process: pull_spec (validate package) -> find -> authorize (reserved names, ownership / trusted publisher) -> verify_gem_scope -> verify_mfa_requirement -> validate (signatures, sigstore) -> save (write gem to storage, purge cache, AfterVersionWriteJob, Rstuf job).

questions.question: Can an author take down a release they already published, and are there limits on which releases can be removed?
questions.answerNote: Deletion (yank) marks the version unindexed and yanked_at, removes from storage/index, purges Fastly and mails owners; eligibility rejects versions older than 30 days or with more than 100,000 downloads (unless forced by admin).

questions.question: How does the site stop people publishing a name that looks like a misspelling of a popular gem?
questions.answerNote: GemTypo#protected_typo? compares names case-insensitively ignoring - and _; a match blocks the push only if the existing gem is protected (>= 10,000 downloads or released within 5 years) and not owned by the pusher, with GemTypoException overrides. Called from Rubygem validation and pending trusted publishers.

questions.question: How are subscribers told when a new version of a gem is released?
questions.answerNote: Version#enqueue_web_hook_jobs fires every enabled gem-specific and global WebHook; WebHook#fire enqueues NotifyWebHookJob, which POSTs the payload through HookRelay with an Authorization header = SHA256(gem name + version + owner api key). Selection starts from an unrelated vendored JS component.

questions.question: How can a CI pipeline publish a gem without a long-lived stored API key?
questions.answerNote: Trusted publishing: CI exchanges its OIDC JWT at api/v1/oidc/trusted_publisher/exchange_token; controller verifies the JWT signature against the provider JWKS and claims, finds the matching trusted publisher (GitHubAction.for_claims matches repository + workflow file from the claims), and mints an API key expiring in 15 minutes.

questions.question: Where are the request rate limits (for logins, pushes, yanks) defined?
questions.answerNote: config/initializers/rack_attack.rb defines Rack::Attack throttles: clearance/ip, exponential backoff levels for API/login/push, api/push/ip, yank/ip, webhook_fire, password reset, etc.

questions.question: Where are the versioned API paths mapped to the controllers that serve them?
questions.answerNote: Rails convention: config/routes.rb namespace :api / namespace :v1 maps resources (rubygems, deletions, owners, web_hooks, oidc/trusted_publisher/exchange_token, ...) to app/controllers/api/v1/*.

questions.question: What rules should I follow when writing a one-off data backfill task?
questions.answerNote: doc/maintenance-tasks.md: limit collection, one record per process call, handle concurrent app writes (conditional update or lock+reload), decide on deleted records, make reruns safe, minimal tests.

c4Note.note: rubygems.org is a Rails MVC app: app/controllers (web + api/v1), app/models (Pusher, Deletion, Version, Rubygem, OIDC), app/jobs (GoodJob/Shoryuken background work), lib/ (compact index, Fastly, gemcutter), plus Postgres, S3 gem storage, Fastly CDN and Elasticsearch/OpenSearch. The scan (symlink-stripped tree) sees only JavaScript: one container with 38 components, all Stimulus controllers under app/javascript and vendored libraries under vendor/javascript (jquery, rails-ujs, stimulus) plus config/tailwind and prettier config. The Ruby application - every model, controller and job - is invisible.
expectedContainers: Rails web + API app (app/controllers, app/models, app/views, config/routes.rb)
Background jobs worker (app/jobs via GoodJob; lib/shoryuken SQS consumer)
PostgreSQL, S3 gem storage, Fastly CDN, search index (external)
Components along domain lines: push/yank (Pusher, Deletion), ownership/orgs, OIDC trusted publishing, webhooks, compact index
problems: No Ruby entities: controllers, models, jobs and lib/ are absent
Vendored third-party JS (vendor/javascript/jquery.js, @hotwired--stimulus.js, rails-ujs...) promoted to first-class components
Config files (config/tailwind.config.js, prettier.config.js) are components next to product code
Single container; web vs job worker split not represented
As-is scan fails on committed symlinks (.claude/skills, config/deploy/*, server/gems)

overviews.note: Scanner-blind but the summary is honest that only the browser-side JS container is mapped, so it can lead; key points are Stimulus-specific; children is one container.
Summary and key points give the Stimulus registration entry and shared application seam; 38 real JS files are a small browsable list; parent redundant.
